findings.title: A box someone else deposited comes back classed received: it ties with real payments and goes first by size, and a register copied as found (d = 1) makes it as public as gap-g1#1's copy
findings.scenario:
Mallory reads Seedelf S1's register off its name and deposits a 5 ₳ box under it byte for byte (d = 1). The wallet holds it as someone else's.

It comes back in one of three ways:
- The user presses Settings' Bring every box back now. Its run takes every box, with no someone-else filter, and its note says nothing of such boxes.
- The user presses Bring one back anyway.
- The pool is later retired, and its run brings every box back.

withdrawOne then seals its way back W as received:<w>. At the next stealth mint or private pool start with no recorded-mixed box that pays alone, Received ranks 1 and one_more sorts by (rank, lovelace). So W (~4.8 ₳) goes before Bob's 20 ₳ payment. The mint spends W, which a withdraw made from a box carrying S1's exact register. Anyone can then tie the new Seedelf to S1, and Mallory learns it. A funding or top-up that W pays alone also takes W first: Fund ranks received 1, before mixed boxes at 2.

gap-g1#1 (a) makes a d = 1 copy paid into the contract Unknown (after received money). But its register match reads only the wallet's contract rows. W's register is fresh, and nothing reads the box's register.

The approved e1a#1 (4) had this way back rank after received money. Round one made it received. Answer 4's plain box (Mint 2) or Unknown (3) would now give that rank.

The same received class also goes to two boxes that may be the user's own session deposit, which anyone can follow:
- a 1.9.1-kept deposit answer with no inputs in a retired pool (rejudge skips retired pools);
- another device's session past GAP_LIMIT.
findings.who: stranger (a deposit fee; the ~5 ₳ stays with the user), plus a bring-back by the user (Settings' button, or anyway) or a later pool retirement

findings.owner_question: Should a box someone else put in under your key come back ranked after money others paid (Unknown, as e1a#1's (4) had it)? Or stay received, with only a d = 1 copy made Unknown?

verdicts.evidence:
Traced on HEAD 5447f7e5, first by reading, then by a Vitest run with the real WebAssembly. The package was built at 20:32, after HEAD's commit at 20:25. I found no guard the finder missed.

1. How the way back is classed. lovejoin.ts:8147 `const received = (await this.someoneElses(network, before, [box])).length > 0;` then :8166-8167 `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : ...`.
   - someoneElsesOf (:2734-2738) only tests which keys paid the deposit.
   - Nothing compares a box's {a, b} with any register. The only callers of registerOf/byRegister are activity.ts:488-493, dapp.ts:2285, balances.ts:548 and contract-scan.ts:468, none in lovejoin.ts.

2. The ways back all reach such a box.
   - Bring every box back now, :7723-7725: `ours = inScope(owned).filter(!madeSince)`, `takes = free(ours, reserved).filter(!tails)`. `free` (:2023) drops only reserved boxes. madeSince (:2337) and tailBoxes (:1570) have no someone-else term. :7787 clears the someoneElse count.
   - Bring one back anyway: withdrawNowNow (:7461-7464) takes the named box when `anyway` is set.
   - A retired pool's run uses the same bringAllBackNow.
   - The only note on the Settings run, settings.lovejoin.privacy.bring, doesn't mention such a box.

3. A Seedelf register is a valid box datum. parse_mix_datum (core lovejoin/mod.rs:409-430) takes Constr 0 [48 bytes, 48 bytes], which is the Register's shape, and is_owned (:498-499) is `a * sk == b`. The withdraw's output is `Register::create(sk)?.rerandomize()` (wasm lovejoin.rs:2759). So the way back W has a fresh datum, and only its input, the box, carries S1's register for anyone to read.

4. Ranks. build.rs:2496-2502, Mint: `Mixed => 0, Received => 1, Lovejoin => 2, Unknown => 3`. :2506-2513, Fund: Received 1, Lovejoin|Mixed 2. Step 1 (:2840-2844) calls one_more, whose :2738 `candidates.sort_by_key(|u| (rank(u), lovelace_of(u)))` tries the smallest first.

5. gap-g1#1 (a)'s copy rule (activity.ts:485-499) only matches a Received row's own register against the view's rows. W's register is fresh, so W stays `received:<tx>`.

6. The run. Setup: a 5 ₳ box whose datum is the Seedelf row a3a3…#0's datum, byte for byte, with a stranger's key paying the deposit. Status lists it under someoneElse.
   - Through bringAllBack + withdrawDue, and through withdrawNow(…, true), the way back is sealed `{"id":"received:<tx>","origin":"received"}` at 4.704978 ₳.
   - The withdraw's inputs include the box.
   - The next stealth mint spends W alone, not Bob's 20 ₳ (b0…#0).

7. The secondary claim holds too. A deposit paid by one-time key 25, with the book at [0], reads as someone else's, and its way back is also sealed `received:<tx>`. Yet someoneElsesOf's comment (:2729-2730) says that case "only leaves its box out of Mix my boxes again", and lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:199-200 calls it "fails safe". The same comment states the retired-pool case as intended.

8. Where the docs meet the code. The reason given for `received` is "never as a box back from Lovejoin, which the stealth mint takes first" (lovejoin.ts:8141-8145, architecture.md:710, lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:9-11 and :252-253). It became false with answer 4: only mixedBox ranks 0, and a plain boxFrom ranks 2, after received money. Round one left e1a#1 (4)'s approved "its box:<tx> class ranks after received money" only because B15 (b) then ranked boxes first. That reason is gone, and today the class ranks ahead of what (4) approved.

9. Nothing discloses it at the mint. mint.privacy.fromPrivate reads "Only boxes back from Lovejoin and money others paid you keep the Seedelf apart from your public account", and a single input draws no merge note.

How far it reaches:
- When the depositor re-randomizes (d ≠ 1), only they can follow W, as with a payment from them. That case only strays from (4)'s words.
- The medium is the d = 1 copy. Anyone can then tie the new Seedelf (or a pool start, or a funding or top-up that W pays alone) to S1, by the wallet's default pick. gap-g1#1 (a) ruled exactly that out for a copy paid into the contract.

Who can cause it: a stranger, for a deposit fee (the box's ADA stays with the user). It then needs the user's bring-back (the Settings run, or anyway) or a pool retirement's automatic run, followed by a stealth mint or pool start from the private balance where W is the smallest single UTxO that pays and no box recorded as mixed pays alone.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Recommended: option 1. At lovejoin.ts:8167, replace `? receivedIn(built.txHash)` with `? unknownIn(built.txHash)`.
- That gives Mint rank 3 and Fund rank 3, tagged Unknown, so it goes after money others paid and after plain boxes, for any d. It needs no register lookup.
- It also covers the two boxes that may be the user's own session deposit and today rank with payments: a 1.9.1 answer with no inputs in a retired pool, and another device's session past GAP_LIMIT.
- I tried it in the copy. The three new cases pass, b15-first-picks.test.ts stays green, and the one failure is the pin at lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:255. That pin flips to `{ id: unknown:${theirs.txHash}, origin: "unknown" }`; update its it() title and the comments at :9-11 and :252-253.

Not recommended: option 2 (keep received, and use Unknown where the box's {a, b} matches a register in the view, Seedelf rows included, via byRegister/registerKey as at activity.ts:488).
- It needs the view inside withdrawOne.
- It catches only registers still in the view, so it misses a removed or spent Seedelf's register.
- It leaves the two own-session cases at received.

One loose end either way. When the private balance pays the way back (`paid: "private"`, a pool whose boxes can't pay their own way), the class is merged with spent.class (:8178). merged() names the class by REACH (histories.ts:121 puts received before unknown), so unknownIn merged with a received UTxO reads as received again. If the d = 1 tie must stay Unknown there too, force origin "unknown" on that merged class for a someone-else box. Otherwise accept it as a stuck-pool edge case.

Words to change with it:
- privacy.md:467: "Brought back, one someone else's key paid is money received, as a payment from whoever put it in would be".
- architecture.md:710: "classed as received (`receivedIn`) … never as a box back from Lovejoin, which the stealth mint takes first". The second half is already stale since answer 4, whichever option is chosen.
- flows.md:519: "brought back, its money is classed as received".
- lovejoin.ts:8141-8145.
- someoneElsesOf's doc at :2729-2730: "which only leaves its box out of Mix my boxes again" is wrong, since its way back is classed too.
- lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:199-200.
- The unreleased 18 November policy entry reads: "For a box back from Lovejoin, it notes whether a mix moved it, or else what put it in: one of your private sessions, or nothing the wallet can tell". It doesn't name the received case today. Add "or someone else", or say that "nothing the wallet can tell" covers it. A change to what's kept belongs in that entry.

The owner's question is as the finding puts it. Option 1 is the private-by-default answer and matches e1a#1 (4)'s "after received money".

verdicts.evidence:
The mechanics hold on HEAD (5447f7e5). I traced them by reading only, with no tests run.

**What the code does**
- lovejoin.ts:8147 `const received = (await this.someoneElses(network, before, [box])).length > 0;` and :8166-8167 `const own = received ? receivedIn(built.txHash) : …`. tests/lovejoin-someone-else.test.ts:255 pins this.
- Every way back takes such a box:
  - Bring every box back now. lovejoin.ts:7723-7725 `takes = free(ours, reserved).filter(...)` has no someone-else filter, and ours() at :3533 lists every owned box.
  - The retired pools' run, which uses the same path.
  - Bring one back anyway. Its warning (lovejoin.anyway.privacy.deposit) says only that anyone can tie that deposit to the private balance.
- Ranks in build.rs:
  - Mint (:2496-2498): `Mixed => 0, Received => 1, Lovejoin => 2`.
  - Fund (:2509-2510): `Received => 1, Lovejoin | Mixed => 2`.
  - :2843 and :2738 sort the singles by (last, rank), then lovelace. Among received money, the smallest UTxO that pays alone goes first.
- The d = 1 copy rule (activity.ts:485-499) checks only rows classed received, against registers in the contract view (`byRegister([...among, ...utxos])`, :488). W's register is fresh (wasm/src/lovejoin.rs:2759/2861/2960 `Register::create(sk)?.rerandomize()`), and nothing reads the pool box's register.

**Where two fixes meet**
- e1a#1 (4), approved, says the way back "ranks after received money".
- Without the received branch, the box falls through to boxFrom. knownOf is true because it has an origins entry. mixedBoxOf is false: the deposit isn't named, it isn't an own leaf, and mixedFor is false. That gives Mint 2 and Fund 2, which is what (4) says.
- Round one chose received only because B15 (b) then ranked every box first. round1.json e1a#1 says so ("needed because B15 (b) makes the stealth mint take boxes first"), and so does DECISIONS note 6.
- Answer 4 removed that reason. The branch now only lifts such a box from Mint 2 to 1 and from Fund 2 to 1.
- Against main (1.9.1: Mint Received 0, Lovejoin 1), the box moves from after payments to tied with them.
- The reason given at lovejoin.ts:8143-8145 and architecture.md:710 ("never as a box back from Lovejoin, which the stealth mint takes first") is now false. A plain box ranks Mint 2, and mixedBoxOf can never be true for a deposit's box.

**Why the impact is below medium**
- **The stranger gains nothing new.** If Mallory pays S1 directly (2-4 ₳, any d), arrived() notes it as received: Mint 1, smallest first. That is the same pick, it's cheaper, and it needs no bring-back.
  - privacy.md:108, :176 and :412 document that link: "whoever paid you knows that UTxO and can tie, in public…".
  - To show it to everyone she only has to reveal her d, which privacy.md:176 says no check catches.
  - The owner approved the d = 1 rule as a narrow extra and said never to word it as protection (DECISIONS gap-g1#1 (2)).
  - So only a careless d = 1 depositor would add exposure, and I know of no tool that deposits into Lovejoin under a register copied as found.
- **The own-box misreads are narrow edges**, and they only move a box from Mint 2 to Mint 1. Without the branch they would be box:<tx>, still ahead of Unknown, Own and Session.
  - A 1.9.1 answer kept with no inputs, for a box still in a retired pool. rejudge at lovejoin.ts:6259 skips `old`, and the retired-pools run since 1.8.0 already brought most such boxes back.
  - Another device's session more than 20 past this device's book.
- **Reach needs several steps by the user:**
  - a bring-back;
  - then a spend from the private balance that W pays alone: a stealth mint (CreateSeedelf.tsx:64 defaults to the public account unless the account is empty), a top-up, or a small funding;
  - with no recorded-mixed box that pays alone.
- **Nothing later catches it.** A single UTxO gives no merge note, and mint.privacy.fromPrivate speaks only of the public account. The UTxOs screen tags W Received, so the user can lock it by hand.
- **A nit-sized wide claim.** privacy.md:467 says the box is received "as a payment from whoever put it in would be". A d = 1 payment would be Unknown while its register is in the view.

findings.scenario:
A user upgrades with a 4.8 ₳ box that 1.9.1 brought back: its withdraw entry has no origin, so classOf reads box:<tx>, origin lovejoin. They also hold Bob's 20 ₳ payment. They read privacy.md:107 ("No payer knows a box back from a mix ... so a box that pays alone goes first, then money you received") and create a Seedelf from the private balance.

Purpose::Mint ranks Lovejoin 2, after Received 1, so step 1 spends Bob's payment. Bob can then tie the new Seedelf to the Seedelf he paid.

The same goes for these, which also come after received money though :107 says a box goes first:
- a box a session deposited and brought back unmixed (session, Mint 5);
- an Unknown way back (3);
- a box a cut chain's own mix moved short of its leaves (plain, 2).

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (5447f7e5). I found no guard the finder missed. The code does what answer 4 asks; three doc lines don't say it.

Code path:
- lovejoin.ts:8166-8174 (withdrawOne): a box's way back gets `mixedBox` (origin "mixed") only when `mixedBoxOf(s, box)` is true (lovejoin.ts:2427-2431: a chain's leaf, or no record plus Koios saying a mix made it). Any other box gets `boxFrom` (histories.ts:59, origin "lovejoin").
- lovejoin.ts:8178 stores `origin` only when it isn't a plain lovejoin box. 1.9.1 stored one only with `spent` or ties (git show web-wallet/1.9.1 lovejoin.ts:7665, :7738).
- So an upgrader's withdraw entry has no origin, and activity.ts:803-804 `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash);` reads it as origin lovejoin.
- Nothing upgrades it later. activity.ts `classes` and script-spend.ts `classesOf`/`readContract` pass it through, and wasm lib.rs:2153 maps "lovejoin" to Origin::Lovejoin.
- build.rs:2496-2503 `Purpose::Mint => match class.origin { Mixed => 0, Received => 1, Lovejoin => 2, Unknown => 3, Own => 4, Session => 5 }`.
- build.rs:2843: step 1 sorts single UTxOs by `(last, rank)` before size, so Bob's payment is tried, and spent, before the old box.
- The review gives no warning. histories.ts:238 `if (classes.length > 1)`: for a one-class spend `historiesNote` says nothing, so CreateSeedelf.tsx:160's HistoriesNote renders nothing.

The docs:
- privacy.md:107: "...so a box that pays alone goes first, then money you received." No qualifier.
- privacy.md:81: "takes a box back from a mix that pays alone first, then received money". A box 1.9.1 brought back after a mix is "a box back from a mix" in plain words, and nothing in privacy.md narrows the phrase.
- architecture.md:137: "`Mint` (...) a box back from Lovejoin, which no payer knows ... then received money".
- These contradict lines that state the rule exactly: privacy.md:172, architecture.md:152 ("every `box:<tx>` written before the mark was kept, which `Mint` ranks after received money"), flows.md:356 and wasm/README.md:56.
- round2b.json confirms neither fixer touched the rank clause. R2-words: "privacy.md :107 (its first clause)" and "the rank clauses are left to R2-b15". R2-b15: "privacy.md:107 and mint.privacy.fromPrivate are R2-words' sentences and I left them as they are".
- The UI string mint.privacy.fromPrivate states no order, so this is words only.
- Existing tests already pin the code: mint_test.rs:3020 a_box_not_recorded_as_mixed_goes_after_received_money, and b15-first-picks.test.ts:375.

Severity medium, by the owner's own scale: "a claim wider than the code". Every box an upgrading user holds is a 1.9.1-era box, and the review is silent when Bob's payment is spent.

findings.title: A private Bootstrap's box comes back marked mixed once its entry closes by count: its deposit boxes sit in the kept leaves, and only public deposits keep their depositor
findings.scenario:
1. The user starts a Bootstrap paid from the private balance (session n). Its chain is its deposit alone, so its c.leaves are the deposit's own, unmixed boxes.
2. RECORD_KEEP_MS (3 h) after it ends, sortOut drops the chain record and keeps its leaves in s.leaves. A public deposit-only chain also gets `depositors`; a private one doesn't.
3. While its MixEntry is open, depositSessionOf finds the entry and the way back is box+session:n, as intended.
4. The entry closes by count with boxes still at its deposit. countBack credits a released Bootstrap with any box no other open mix takes (`?? released[0]`): a restore's or another device's, say. squareUp's last pass also counts Bootstraps back for boxes at their deposit. update then drops closed entries.
5. The rest are free now and come back. depositSessionOf finds no chain, no entry and no Koios answer (s.leaves makes them recorded, so Koios isn't asked). knownOf is true, and mixedBoxOf finds them in ownLeaves, so the way back gets mixedBox, Mint 0.

The next stealth mint or private pool start takes that box first. Anyone can follow it from the deposit to session n's one-time account and its funding.

This is time#1's named path ("a private Bootstrap's released boxes that nobody has mixed"), now fixed only while the entry lives. Before this round it read as a plain box; now it carries the mark 'a mix moved it'. privacy.md:434 says a private Bootstrap's box is that session's money.

When a private deposit-only chain's record goes, keep its deposit too, e.g. `depositors[c.deposit] = { session: c.session, seen }`. depositAccountOf then takes only entries with `account`, and depositSessionOf reads the new entries. Or don't move a deposit-only chain's leaves into s.leaves at all.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 5447f7e5. I found no guard that stops it, and a test reproduces it end to end, including the stealth mint's pick.

I'm raising it from low to medium. There is a more ordinary trigger than the finder's "a restore's or another device's box": two Bootstraps in one pool, the older one private, released together by Bring them all back, after other people's mixes moved a box of the younger one (which is what a Bootstrap is for). The user alone causes it. It is also a regression from shipped 1.9.1 in this case. 1.9.1's Purpose::Mint had `Received => 0, Lovejoin => 1`, so this box's way back went after money others paid. Now it goes first.

**How it happens**
1. A Bootstrap is depth 0, so its chain's leaves are its deposit's own boxes. In core lovejoin/mod.rs fan_out, `leaves: ours` with `ours = start` when no waves run.
2. After RECORD_KEEP_MS, sortOut moves every dropped chain's leaves into `s.leaves`, owner "session.<n>" (lovejoin.ts:6330). It keeps the deposit in `depositors` only for public chains: `if (keep(c) || c.session !== undefined || !c.deposit || c.mixes.length) continue;` (:6338). keep(c) (:6297) never looks at the entry, and unmixedOf counts the deposit's boxes as leaves, so the record goes while the entry still holds them.
3. countBack (:2586-2597) builds `released = bootstrap ? [] : openIn(s, p, true).filter((e) => e.released)` and picks `target = unmixed ?? its ?? candidates.find(...) ?? candidates[0] ?? released[0]`. openIn sorts oldest first (:2563). So any returned box that isn't at a deposit is credited to the oldest released Bootstrap when no other mix is open, another Bootstrap's moved box included.
4. backOrder (:2222) brings back boxes in `ownLeaves` last, so moved boxes come back before the kept deposit boxes. update drops closed entries (:8602).
5. The older Bootstrap's entry closes while its own box still sits at its deposit. withdrawOne (:8165-8174) then runs, with these results:
   - `received` is false: someoneElsesOf goes through depositsOf, which needs `!known`, and `s.leaves` makes the box known.
   - depositSessionOf (:2399-2408) finds no chain, no entry and no origin. found() (:6427) and made() never ask Koios about a recorded box.
   - knownOf is true. depositsNamed (:2410-2419) no longer names the deposit.
   - mixedBoxOf (:2427-2431) hits `ownLeaves(s).has(ref(b))`, so the class is `mixedBox`.
6. build.rs:2494-2501 ranks `Purpose::Mint` `Mixed => 0`; the right class `box:<w>+session:n` reads as session, which ranks 5. Fund now ranks the box 2 instead of 5. The escape hatch's private payer (:8085) takes it first too.
7. This contradicts privacy.md:434 ("A box brought back from where a private session's deposit put it is that session's money… a private Bootstrap's") and privacy-policy.md:93 ("only a box a mix moved is what a Seedelf or a pool's start takes first"). The public case got this exact count edge fixed as 316#1 (privacy.md:433). The private case didn't.

**Guards I checked and ruled out:** received/someoneElses, origins and the Koios lookups, depositAccountOf (it keeps the deposit for public chains only), keep(c), any exclusion for deposit-only chains in ownLeaves, and the read sanitizer.

The fix sketch below, applied in the copy, makes both tests pass. 62 Lovejoin-related test files (1115 tests) passed with it, and tsc was clean apart from the test file.
verdicts.fix_notes:
Keep a private deposit-only chain's deposit as 316#1 keeps a public one. All of this is in lovejoin.ts and was checked in a copy:

1. **Schedule.depositors type (:1019).** Change it to `Record<string, { account?: number; session?: number; seen: number }>`. Update its doc (:1011-1018) to say "the public account, or private session, whose deposit…".
2. **sortOut loop (:6337-6340).** Drop `c.session !== undefined ||` from the skip test and write:
   `(s.depositors ??= {})[c.deposit] ??= c.session === undefined ? { account: c.account ?? 0, seen: now } : { session: c.session, seen: now };`
   Retype the flatMap at :6341 as `Array<[string, NonNullable<Schedule["depositors"]>[string]]>`. Reword the comment at :6334 to cover a private session's deposit.
3. **depositSessionOf (:2402-2403).** After the entry lookup, add:
   `const kept = s.depositors?.[b.txHash]; if (kept) return kept.session;`
4. **Read sanitizer (:8490).** Accept either key: `(Number.isInteger(d.account) || Number.isInteger(d.session))`. Without this, the next read drops the new entry and the fix silently does nothing.
5. **Already right, no change needed:**
   - depositAccountOf's `if (kept) return kept.account;` returns undefined for a session's entry.
   - depositsNamed, mixedBoxOf and someoneElsesOf already read the depositors keys.
   - Fix depositsNamed's doc, which says "a public one's".
6. **Docs.**
   - privacy.md:434: add the line :433 has: "The deposit keeps that tie once its chain's record and its mix are gone, so every such box is the session's however its mix's count closes."
   - architecture.md:152: mention the kept deposit.
   - Privacy policy: nothing new in kind is kept, because `s.leaves` already names "session.<n>" for that box. If the owner's rule wants it stated, add a clause to the 18 November entry.

**Fix I don't recommend:** leaving a deposit-only chain's leaves out of `s.leaves`. The box would then read as unrecorded, so Koios gets asked about it (a new request) and it's held as not mixed yet (depositsOf). That changes how Bootstraps hold their boxes, which the depositors doc already warns about.

**Tests.** Add the two tests below, e.g. to tests/b15-first-picks.test.ts. With the fix, change `expect(after.depositors).toBeUndefined()` to `expect(after.depositors?.[D]).toMatchObject({ session: 4 })`.

- `withdraw.ts:219-220` (blame: 9f8df1b1):
  `const paidFor = (await classesOf(this.deps, network, [utxo]))[...]; const origin = merged([...(paidFor ? [paidFor] : []), leftBy(rest.txHash)]);`
- `classesOf` reads `activity.classes` with `utxos = [utxo]`. So `known` is worked out over that one Seedelf row (`activity.ts:481-483`).
- A Seedelf whose mint this device never recorded comes back as bare `UNKNOWN`. That covers a restore, the CLI and another profile; `arrived()` never writes an entry for a Seedelf row (`activity.ts:571`).
- `script-spend.ts:277` then drops it: `filter(([, c]) => c.id !== UNKNOWN.id)`. So the removal seals `change:<removeTx>` alone.
- Every other `leftBy` caller (mint.ts:135, transfer.ts:171, withdraw.ts:165, lovejoin-launch.ts:364) goes through `changeHistory`, which keeps `UNKNOWN` for unfound inputs (script-spend.ts:168-173). So only the removal makes a class with nothing but `change:` parts.
- `histories.ts:228-251` counts `box:`, `received:`, `public:`, unknown/elsewhere and `session:` parts (`sessionsIn`, :149-150). It counts no `change:` part.
- `listed([])` returns `""` (:188). The together sentence is pushed whenever `classes.length > 1` (:238-256), with no check for an empty list.
- No guard downstream: HistoriesNote.tsx renders what it gets, and Withdraw.tsx:235 and Transfer.tsx:246 pass `summary.histories` straight through.

Run result:
- Two Seedelfs with no mint entry, removed into the balance, sealed `{"id":"change:81b9…","origin":"session"}` and `{"id":"change:c59f…","origin":"session"}`.
- A 15 ₳ Send merged both, and its note reads: "This spends  together. Anyone can see they're one owner's, which ties them to each other."
- Max reads: "Sending everything spends  together. …"
- es and ja use the same template shape, so they break the same way ("a la vez ." in es).
- A payment received plus one such removal's money gives "This spends a payment you received together. …"

Before round two (69d001e8) such a removal kept no origin (`...(origin ? { origin } : {})`). Its money then read as Unknown: no note while nothing else was known, or "money from 2 transactions the wallet has no history for" once anything was. This contradicts privacy.md:169 (a removal's change "keeps its inputs' histories, merged") and :173 ("the review says what's spent together").

**(b) The change kind is missing: older note code, which R2-b15 named as residue ("true, but clumsy")**
- `historiesNote([payment, change of mint M that spent box B])` is byte-identical to `historiesNote([payment, a fresh box B])`: "This spends a box back from Lovejoin and a payment you received together. … and undoes some of what Lovejoin did for the box."
- It never says this also ties the earlier spend, and through it the Seedelf that mint made.
- A session's unmixed box (`box:w+session:n`, lovejoin.ts:8169) gets the 'undoes' clause too. Unmixed boxes got that clause before round two as well. The id can't tell it from a funding's change that spent a mixed box (sessions.ts:3196), so that part is a nit.

- No stranger, no site, no funds at risk. Selection still merges only when nothing else pays.
- What breaks is the words of a privacy note in an edge case, so low.

findings.title: For a stealth mint, money made private now goes before an earlier spend's change, so when nothing fresher pays, the new Seedelf is tied to the public account rather than to an earlier Seedelf
findings.scenario:
The private balance holds 50 ₳ made private from account 0 (public:0, Mint 4). It also holds about 7.7 ₳ of change from S1, which was created from a 10 ₳ box or from Bob's payment (box:B+change:M or received:bob+change:M, origin session, Mint 5). There's no recorded-mixed box and no payment received.

Creating S2 from the private balance, step 1 takes the 50 ₳ (rank 4) before the change (rank 5). Anyone can then tie S2 to the public account.

mint.privacy.fromPrivate says only boxes and money others paid keep the Seedelf apart from the public account. The change would have tied S2 to S1, not to the account. In 1.9.1 that change went first, read as a box or as received money.

Answer 2 puts change after fresh money. It doesn't say whether money made private counts as fresh for a stealth mint. REACH puts change in the session tier, after Own.
findings.who: nobody (the wallet's default pick)
findings.evidence:

histories.ts:79 `leftBy = (txHash) => ({ id: change:${txHash}, origin: "session" })`
histories.ts:121 REACH `["session", "own", "received", "lovejoin", "unknown"]`

findings.owner_question: For a stealth mint, when nothing fresher pays, which link should the wallet make: tie the new Seedelf to your public account (money made private), or to an earlier Seedelf (its change)?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 5447f7e5, traced end to end. I found no guard that stops it.

How a stealth mint's change is classed:
- mint.ts:135 seals the change as `merged([changeHistory(classes, finished.inputs), leftBy(finished.txHash)])`.
- histories.ts:79 defines `leftBy` as `{ id: change:<tx>, origin: "session" }`, and originOf (:115) maps `change:` to "session".
- merged() (:145) takes the first origin in REACH order (:121 `["session","own",...]`). So any class with a `change:` part reads "session". Both `box:B+change:M` and `change:M+received:bob` do (ids are sorted, so the finding's `received:bob+change:M` is really spelled `change:M+received:bob`).

How the WebAssembly and core rank it:
- The WebAssembly takes the sealed origin as given (lib.rs:2149-2156 `"session" => Origin::Session`), and mint_spend passes Purpose::Mint (lib.rs:2546). The private pool start does too (:2857).
- Core ranks Purpose::Mint as `Mixed 0, Received 1, Lovejoin 2, Unknown 3, Own 4, Session 5` (build.rs:2496-2503).
- Step 1 sorts singles by `(last(u), purpose.rank(&class(u)))` (build.rs:2843), and one_more then sorts by (rank, lovelace). So the 50 ₳ `public:0` (Own, written by move-in.ts:124 madePrivate) is tried before the 7.7 ₳ change and pays alone.

Nothing tells the user at review:
- spentHistories gives `[public:0]`, and historiesNote returns undefined for one class and one account.
- Only the form's static callout, mint.privacy.fromPrivate, speaks to it.
- The only way to steer is coin control: the UTxOs screen tags Made private and Change, and the user can lock a row.

What 1.9.1 did, and when it changed:
- At the web-wallet/1.9.1 tag, mint.ts:132 sealed `changeHistory` alone, so the change was `box:B` (Lovejoin) or `received:bob` (Received). Mint ranked `Received 0, Lovejoin 1, Unknown 2, Own 3, Session 4`, so the change went first and S2 was tied to S1, not to the account.
- Round one (69d001e8) did the same. The flip came with 9f8df1b1, the answer-2 commit.

Why this is undecided rather than the owner's call:
- Answer 2 was asked with "fresh money (a box back, a payment received)".
- The verifiers left Own against change open: money#2's said "before Unknown/Own/Session, or after Own if the owner wants", and own#1's said "at Own's or Session's rank".
- The fixer's own commit message only claims "money others paid, and a box a mix moved, before it". The order Own before change came from reusing Session's rank.

The docs are silent, not wrong. privacy.md:81, :171 and :172 and the policy's 18 November entry only say change goes after money others paid and after a mixed box. That's true, so no claim is wider than the code.

Siblings with the same trade:
- A private pool start uses Purpose::Mint.
- Purpose::Fund ranks Own 4 before Session 5, and also gives change tier 1 when merging. In 1.9.1 a box-paid or received-paid change went before Own for both.

Both tests below fail on HEAD. The control passes: change that names `public:0` stays after plain Own.

Why low: each choice makes some tie, it only happens when no mixed box or received payment pays, and no doc promise breaks. If the owner rules that the public-account tie is the worse one, this is a medium-class default that went backwards from 1.9.1.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Put the finder's question to the owner first, and widen it to the siblings: a stealth mint, a private pool start (both Purpose::Mint) and a funding (Purpose::Fund). When nothing fresher pays, should the wallet tie the new Seedelf (or start, or session) to the public account through money made private, or to the earlier spend through its change?

2. If the owner says keep the public account out:

  - Pay: rank Change with Session (1).

findings.title: A page counted while still on its way to the connect question spares the site, and if it leaves before it asks, no back-off is ever recorded
findings.scenario:
1. Tab A of https://dex.example has its connect question in the window.
2. Tab B of the same site calls enable(). Its call is counted in `enabling` as soon as it reaches call() (:584). It then waits in its first reads: preferences.get, wallet.state on the wallet's queue, needsPassword, and the sealed `dapps` read in site().
3. A goes away (a reload or a closed tab). gone(A) finds B live in `enabling` (:936), so it doesn't call refuseFor (:938). A's question is removed and the window closes.
4. B goes away before its enable() reaches the asking branch. gone(B) finds no waiting entry and no unlock wait of B's own, so it returns at :929 after only marking B gone.
5. B's call then ends with PAGE_GONE at unlocked() (:1593) or ask() (:1632-1633). Nothing is asked and nothing is recorded.
6. Neither departure records the back-off, so the site's next page (A reloaded) asks at once, and the window comes back right after both pages left.

At 69d001e8 this order did record it: gone(A) counted only `sharedBy`, which a page joined at the sharing branch, so refuseFor ran. The docs say the sparing page "asks itself" (architecture.md:563, flows.md:436, privacy.md:349), but here it never does.

A site can arrange this on purpose: tab B calls enable() and reloads, and tab A reloads right after B's message (BroadcastChannel). It can repeat this. It can also happen by chance, when the user closes a window holding both tabs while B's enable() is on its way.

No funds or privacy are at stake. The question is the same connect question, and closing the window still counts as a decline that backs off. B7's exception already lets a site's second page re-ask, so the nuisance is no worse than what the owner accepted.
findings.who: a site (two coordinated tabs), or ordinary timing (closing a window that holds two of the site's tabs)
findings.evidence:

dapp.ts:934-938 `const live = (id: string) => id !== session.id && !this.gonePages.has(id); const shared = [...(this.enabling.get(session.origin)?.keys() ?? [])].some(live) || this.unlocking.some((u) => u.session.origin === session.origin); if (!shared) this.refuseFor(...)`
dapp.ts:1632-1633 (ask) `// Its page went away while it was read ... if (this.gonePages.has(session.id)) throw refused(PAGE_GONE);`
At 69d001e8 the clause was `[...(question?.sharedBy ?? [])].some(live)`, with sharedBy filled only at enable()'s sharing branch.
tests/dapp-gone.test.ts:390-404 ('turns it away once every page that shared the question has gone') covers only gone(second) before gone(first). The three new sign#3 cases (:284, :321, :350) all keep the second page alive. Neither covers first-then-second with the second still on its way.
findings.fix:
Carry the spare to the page that gave it:
- When gone() is spared only by pages in `enabling` that have no question or unlock wait of their own, keep a per-origin mark `spared.set(origin, { title, network })`.
- Clear the mark when a page of that origin reaches ask() for a connect question, or connects.
- In gone()'s early-return path for a page in `enabling`, and in call()'s finally when a gone page's enable() ends: if the origin is still marked and no other live page is in `enabling`, call refuseFor(origin, title, network) and clear the mark.

Test (dapp-gone): the first page asks. Hold the second's sealed `dapps` read (as at :291-301). Call gone(first), then gone(second), then release. enableMeets(t) should give DECLINED_WAIT, and declined() should list the origin.
findings.owner_question: When the page that spared the site leaves without ever asking, should the back-off land then (as it did at 69d001e8 for this order), or is an immediate re-ask after both pages have left acceptable?

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds. I traced it on HEAD 5447f7e5 (fixes tree, left clean) and found no guard the finder missed.

How it happens:
1. `call()` counts the page in `enabling` before any await: dapp.ts:584 `if (method === "enable") this.countEnabling(session, 1);`.
2. gone(A), A holding its question: `shared` comes out true because `enabling` holds B, and B is live (not A, not in gonePages) (:934-936). So :938's `refuseFor` doesn't run. A's entry is removed and rejected with PAGE_GONE.
3. gone(B): `if (this.pageCalls.has(session.id)) this.gonePages.add(session.id)`. B has no `waiting` or `unlocking` entry, so it returns at :929. Nothing on that path looks at `enabling`.
4. B's call goes on:
   - Unlocked: no `asking` at :1135 (A's entry is gone), `refusing(origin)` is false at :1151, and `ask()` throws PAGE_GONE at :1633.
   - Locked: `unlocked()` throws PAGE_GONE at :1594. The finding's :1593 is the comment line above it.
5. No other path records the back-off. `refuseFor` is called only from `answer()` :740, `windowClosed()` :837 and `gone()` :938. `windowClosed()` returns early when nothing waits (:810-813).

Reachability: sw.ts:433-435 calls `gone()` from each port's disconnect, in a task of its own. So "A leaves, then B leaves while B is still in its awaits" can happen. The window is milliseconds when the wallet is idle, and up to about 1 s during a contract scan (sign#3's verifier measured this).

Tests, on a copy of HEAD:
- The three new cases fail: unlocked with B held in its sealed `dapps` read, locked with B held at its first preferences read, and B already at the sharing branch leaving while it runs `enable()` again.
- The control, B leaving first, passes. The 14 existing dapp-gone tests pass.

History, with 69d001e8's dapp.ts swapped in:
- Both on-its-way cases pass there: B wasn't in `sharedBy`, so gone(A) refused. The control passes too.
- The sharing-branch case fails at 69d001e8 as well.
- So the finding's "69d001e8 did record it" is right for a page still on its way. The same no-back-off outcome already existed after round one, for a page that reached the sharing branch and left while running `enable()` again. Round two widened it to every page from `call()`'s first line.

Severity: low, as the finder says.
- No funds or privacy are involved.
- A site gains nothing new. Under B7's accepted exception, two tabs taking turns already keep a question up with no back-off, and every re-ask calls `window.show()`, which focuses the window (`focused`, `drawAttention`; dapp-window.ts:20-25).
- By accident, closing a window that holds both tabs leaves no page to ask again.
- Docs: architecture.md:563 and flows.md:436 say the sparing page "asks itself", and here it never does. privacy.md:349 says such a site is kept, and it isn't. That keeps less than the doc says, so it isn't a privacy overclaim.

Found while building the fix: landing the refusal in gone(B) alone lets B's still-running call reach `refusing(origin)` in `enable()` (:1151) and in `unlocked()` (:1589). Both checks come before any `gonePages` check, so `askedAgain` sets `retried: true`, and the lists would say "and it asked again" for a page that has already left. A probe confirmed this. The same already happens today in the control order.
verdicts.fix_notes:
A prototype in the copy passed dapp-gone and 14 other dApp test files (192 tests), and `tsc --noEmit` was clean. Every edit is in extension/src/background/dapp.ts.

1. Add a field: `private readonly spared = new Map<string, { title?: string; network?: NetworkName }>();`. It holds sites whose decline a page in `enabling` spared.
2. Move gone()'s `live`/`shared` (:934-937) into `private sharedBeyond(session)`. It returns true when another live page of the site is in `enabling`, or any page of the site is in `unlocking`.
3. In gone():
   - Not shared: call `refuseFor` as now.
   - Shared: record `this.spared.set(origin, { title: session.title, ...(network ? { network } : {}) })`, where `network` is `question?.network ?? unlocking[0]?.network`.
   - In the early-return path (:929), before returning: land the decline if all of these hold:
     - `this.spared.get(origin)` is set;
     - `this.enabling.get(origin)?.has(session.id)`;
     - `!this.sharedBeyond(session)`;
     - no connect question (`!connected`) of the site is in `waiting`.
     Landing means `this.refuseFor(origin, spared.title, spared.network); this.deps.changed();`.
4. Clear the mark in these places:
   - At the top of `refuseFor`: any refusal uses it up.
   - In `ask()`, right after the push, when `request.kind === "connect"` and the request isn't `connected`.

findings.title: Bring every box back now, and the retired pools' run, bring a box someone else's mix moved back as Unknown, never asked about, so it loses the box's tag, tier and note
findings.scenario:
Steady state on mainnet or preprod: the user's boxes sit in v2's 5 ₳ pool, and other people's mixes have moved them to outpoints no record names. The M14 count holds, so no read asks Koios about them: found() asks only when moreThanDue or for `asking` (6433). The user presses Settings → Bring every box back now, or a pool page's every-box button. bringAllBackNow takes every box in scope (7723) and calls withdrawOne (7835) without asking about any of them. withdrawDue asks about the one box it takes first (made(), 7324-7328); this path doesn't. In withdrawOne, `received` is false, depositSessionOf finds nothing, and `!knownOf(s)(box) && !depositsNamed(s).has(box.txHash)` holds, so every way back is sealed as unknown:<w>.

What follows:
(a) The UTxOs screen tags each one Unknown, though Activity lists it Back from Lovejoin.
(b) Its class depends on the button. The same box left to come back by itself is asked about and marked `mixed`, Mint rank 0. Brought back this way it ranks 3, so a pool's start (private by default) or a stealth mint takes received money (rank 1) and plain boxes (2) first.
(c) tier() gives Unknown 0, not 2, so these boxes no longer come "last, one at a time". A spend merging two of them reads "money from 2 transactions the wallet has no history for", with no "undoes some of what Lovejoin did for the boxes".
(d) Where none of a spend's candidates has a known history, classes() collapses them all into one UNKNOWN class (classOfRow). A 7 ₳ Send from three 4.7 ₳ ways back then merges two of them with the CLI's order and no note at all.

At 69d001e8 each of these was box:<w>: kept apart, merged last, and named in the note.

Where two fixes meet: time#1's verifier proposed Unknown for "can't tell" because round one ranked Lovejoin first for Mint. Answer 4 has since moved a plain box after received money, and core's Origin::Lovejoin doc now describes exactly such a box. The reason for Unknown is gone, and the side effects stay.

Docs it breaks: privacy.md:168 says Unknown only for a box brought back before any mix moved it, and :172 says boxes back from Lovejoin come last, one at a time. architecture.md:714-715 still says a retired pool's answer "decides nothing", but it now decides `mixed` versus Unknown.

and :8178 writes it, since `own.origin !== "lovejoin"`.

- `s.origins` is written only by lookUp (:6492) and rejudge (:6603). lookUp is reached only from found() and made().

Order a already puts Unknown (rank 3) after Own, Session and Received, and boxes are grown one at a time after that. The selection harm is the missing or wrong note and the Mint and pool-start pick, not extra merging.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 5447f7e5. I traced it end to end, found no guard the finder missed, and reproduced it with the real WebAssembly. The package was built at 20:32, after HEAD's 20:25 commit.

**1. What gets sealed.** In withdrawOne, lovejoin.ts:8166-8178 reads `: !knownOf(s)(box) && !depositsNamed(s).has(box.txHash) ? unknownIn(built.txHash)`, and then `origin = spent || received || own.origin !== "lovejoin" ? ... : undefined`. So a box with no record and no origins answer is written as `{id: unknown:<w>, origin: unknown}`.
- At 69d001e8 it was `own = received ? receivedIn(..) : boxFrom(..)` with `origin = spent || received ? merged(..) : undefined`. With no origin written, activity.ts:803 `case "lovejoin-withdraw": return boxFrom(entry.txHash)` gave `box:<w>`, lovejoin.
- Nothing re-classes it later. settleWithdrawing (:8380) re-writes `w.origin`, activity.sent writes the entry once, and nothing maps a later Koios answer back onto the withdraw's entry.
- WebAssembly maps origin strings only (lib.rs:2153-2155). Nothing in the worker or in WebAssembly treats a lovejoin-withdraw entry as a box apart from its class.

**2. Selection.**
- activity.ts:481-483: when every row is Unknown, every row becomes UNKNOWN.
- script-spend.ts classesOf drops UNKNOWN ids, so build.rs select_script_inputs is blind and takes the CLI's order: pure ADA, largest first.
- Once anything is known, build.rs:2522-2528 `tier()` puts Unknown at 0 and Lovejoin/Mixed at 2, and Pay ranks Unknown 3. The by_history sort (:2913) is (last, tier, !joins_base, rank, …), so the way backs come after own, session and received money but before any box.
- `is_box` (:2934) needs tier 2, so these way backs never go through 'as few boxes as pay'.
- histories.ts:228/:231 count only `box:` parts as boxes, so the note drops `lovejoinUndone`.

**3. How the state is reached.**
- (a) Bring one back anyway: withdrawNowNow sets `force` only `if (!anyway && !known(chosen))`, and the unsure/untold refusal is skipped with anyway (:7461-7476).
- (b) A retired pool: sortOut :6266 `waits` keeps unsure boxes free, and the due withdraw skips the question there (:7324).
- (c) A third path the finder missed: Bring every box back now (bringAllBackNow) takes `free(ours, reserved)` minus tails and never asks Koios.
- Each needs Koios and the data layer silent about the box's making at the way back, or the user's own anyway.

**4. Docs and round-two notes.** privacy.md:172 says 'boxes back from Lovejoin come last, one at a time', while :168 and :434 and architecture.md:152 say the way back is Unknown. Round2b's own#4 'left' and the lead's residue both named this trade-off ('an Unknown way back is Pay rank 3, tier 0, so a Send may merge it sooner than it would a box'), and it never reached the owner as a question.

**5. Reproduced: 3 tests fail on HEAD.**
- In a restored wallet (4 ₳ Unknown found at the first reading, then two boxes brought back anyway with tx_info at 500), the way back's class reads the bare `unknown`.
- A Send of one box plus 0.1 ₳ spends both way backs together, and the review note is undefined: nothing is said.
- After Bob's 10 ₳ lands, a Send of 10 ₳ plus one box plus 0.3 ₳ spends Bob's payment and both way backs, leaving the 4 ₳ Unknown row. The note reads 'This spends a payment you received and money from 2 transactions the wallet has no history for together…', with no Lovejoin clause.

findings.title: A private Bootstrap's never-mixed box reads as a mix's leaf once its chain record and its mix entry are gone, so it's marked mixed and becomes the stealth mint's first pick
findings.scenario: A private Bootstrap (session 4) leaves box D#0 at its deposit, never mixed. A Bootstrap's leaves are its deposit's own boxes (b15 fixture: `mixes: [], leaves: [inAda(D)]`), so unmixedOf is empty. keep() (:6297-6298) drops the chain record 3 h after it ended, and :6330 moves D#0 into `s.leaves`. Its entry then closes by count while D#0 is still there. countBack (:2595) counts a box from a restore or another device against `released[0]`, the released Bootstrap, and closed entries are dropped at :8602. 316#1 found this for public deposits, and `s.depositors` keeps those, but only `c.session === undefined` ones (:6338). When D#0 comes back, depositSessionOf (:2399-2407) finds no chain, no entry and no origin, since a recorded box is never asked about. knownOf is true through s.leaves, depositsNamed lacks D, and mixedBoxOf returns true through ownLeaves. The way back is sealed mixedBox: Mint rank 0. The next stealth mint or private pool start takes it first, and anyone can follow it from the Bootstrap's deposit to session 4's funding. That is the time#1/still#1 class this round closed for chains and entries. The policy's new 'only a box a mix moved is what a Seedelf or a pool's start takes first' (privacy-policy.md:93) is false here.
findings.who: Nobody's action beyond an extra box (a restore's, another device's) counted against a released private Bootstrap: a narrow state the wallet reaches by itself.
findings.evidence: lovejoin.ts:2428-2429 `if (depositsNamed(s).has(b.txHash)) return false;` / `if (ownLeaves(s).has(ref(b))) return true;`; :2450 `ownLeaves = (s) => new Set([...s.chains.flatMap((c) => c.leaves.map(ref)), ...Object.keys(s.leaves ?? {})])`; :6330 `const gone = s.chains.filter((c) => !keep(c)).flatMap((c) => c.leaves.map((l) => [ref(l), ownerOf(c)] as const));`; :6338 `if (keep(c) || c.session !== undefined || !c.deposit || c.mixes.length) continue;`; :2595 `… ?? candidates[0] ?? released[0];`; :8602 `schedule.mixes = (schedule.mixes ?? []).filter(open);`. The time#1 impact verifier warned not to read 'mixed' from records that count a chain's own deposit box (review1.json fix_notes).
findings.fix: Keep a private no-mix chain's deposit after its record goes, as `depositors` does for a public one. In the loop at :6337-6340, also record `{ session: c.session, seen }` where `c.session !== undefined && !c.mixes.length`. Have depositSessionOf read it, and depositAccountOf skip entries with no account, so depositsNamed names the deposit and the way back is `box:<w>+session:4`. Alternatively, count a kept leaf as mixed only where its chain had mixes, which means keeping that bit with the leaf. Test: a schedule with no chain, no entry and `leaves: { 'D#0': 'session.4' }`; bringing D#0 back must not give origin 'mixed'.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD (5447f7e5). I traced it end to end, found no guard, and reproduced it through the worker with the real WebAssembly (wasm/pkg built 20:32, after the last core/wasm commit at 20:25).

1. A private Bootstrap's leaves are its deposit's own boxes.
- Core's fan_out at depth 0 returns `leaves: ours`, which are the start boxes (seedelf-core/src/lovejoin/mod.rs:2646-2697).
- sessions.ts:5506-5516 records `session`, `bootstrap` and those leaves.
- entryOf (lovejoin.ts:2532-2543) keeps `deposit` and `session` on the entry.

2. The record goes and the box becomes a kept leaf.
- keep() (:6297-6298) keeps the record only while `unmixedOf([c], listed)` is non-empty, and unmixedOf (:2062-2066) skips leaves. So the record goes 3 h after it ended (or after its delay's least).
- :6330 then moves D#0 into `s.leaves` as "session.4".
- :6338 `if (keep(c) || c.session !== undefined || ...) continue;` keeps a depositor for public chains only.

3. The entry closes by count while D#0 is still there.
- After Bring them all back (releaseBootstrap :6989-6993), D#0 is free.
- backOrder (:2219-2224) puts a kept leaf after a box that isn't one, so another box X goes first.
- countBack (:2586-2598) finds no record that made X and no deposit it sits at. With no other mix open in that pool, :2595 `... ?? candidates[0] ?? released[0]` counts X against the Bootstrap.
- The update then drops the closed entry (:8602).
- The code already knows this path: the depositors comment (:1010-1018) says "another box counted first closes one early (316#1)".

4. D#0's way back is marked mixed. In withdrawOne (:8146-8176):
- `received` is false: someoneElsesOf goes through depositsOf, which skips recorded boxes.
- `told` is undefined: found() asks only about `!known(b)` boxes (:6427-6428), and recorded() (:2073-2076) counts `s.leaves`.
- depositSessionOf (:2399-2407) finds no chain, no entry and no origin.
- knownOf is true. mixedBoxOf (:2427-2431): depositsNamed lacks D, and ownLeaves (:2450) has D#0, so the result is `mixedBox`.
- build.rs:2496-2503 ranks Mint `Mixed => 0`, against `Session => 5`.

5. Guards I looked for, none of which stops it:
- squareUp can't close a Bootstrap whose box is listed: the listed box offsets its own count.
- The never-landed rule needs `!e.found`.
- moveOn skips Bootstraps.
- Nothing asks Koios about D#0 again.
- Without the release, `released` is empty and countBack finds no target. So the release is a precondition, as the finding says.

6. Reproduced (test below):
- Test A drives the whole path. The record drops, `leaves` = {D#0: "session.4"}, X comes back first and closes the entry while D#0 is listed, and D#0's way back is `{box:<w>, mixed}`.
- Test C starts from the state 1.9.1 already leaves on devices (record gone, entry open) and fails the same way.
- Test B: a stealth mint with that way back beside Bob's 60 ₳ payment spends the way back.
- So privacy-policy.md:93 ("only a box a mix moved is what a Seedelf or a pool's start takes first") and privacy.md:168 are wider than the code here.

Who can cause it: the user's own Bring them all back, plus any box in that pool that no open mix accounts for. That box can come from another device on the same phrase, or from a stranger who deposits under the user's register and mixes it herself (own#3's case). No other non-Bootstrap mix can be open in that pool, or it absorbs the count. With k boxes, each extra box counted first leaves one of the Bootstrap's last boxes marked as mixed.

Low: the precondition is narrow, but the effect is a link made by default.
verdicts.fix_notes:
1. Extend `depositors` (316#1's mechanism) to a private no-mix chain's deposit:
   - lovejoin.ts:1019 type becomes `{ account?: number; session?: number; seen: number }`. Update its comment at :1010-1018.
   - :6337-6340: drop `c.session !== undefined ||` and write `c.session === undefined ? { account: c.account ?? 0, seen: now } : { session: c.session, seen: now }`.
   - :6341: the prune's type annotation.
   - :8490, the read normalizer: accept `Number.isInteger(d.account) || Number.isInteger(d.session)`. Without this, the next read drops the new entries.
   - depositSessionOf (:2399-2407): after the entry check, add `const kept = s.depositors?.[b.txHash]; if (kept) return kept.session;`.
   - depositAccountOf (:2385-2386) needs no change: `return kept.account` is undefined for a session's entry. depositsNamed and someoneElsesOf already read depositors' keys.

2. Backfill. 1.9.1 already dropped every held private Bootstrap's record 3 h after it ended. So on update, most are "no chain, entry open, box in s.leaves", and the chain loop never sees them. In the same sortOut update, also write from open entries:
   `for (const e of entries(s)) if ((e.bootstrap || e.seed) && e.session !== undefined && e.deposit) (s.depositors ??= {})[e.deposit] ??= { session: e.session, seen: now };`
   Use `e.deposit` only, never depositOf's `e.id` fallback: a private Bootstrap's id is its return's.

3. One gap remains. An entry that already closed under 1.9.1 with its box still out leaves only `s.leaves`, which can't be told from a mix's leaf. So test B (the finding's own suggested fixture: no chain, no entry, `leaves: {D#0: 'session.4'}`) still fails under 1+2. Choose one:

   - Also take the finding's alternative: count a kept leaf as mixed only where a bit written from this release says its chain had mixes (for example, a kept set of such leaves next to `s.leaves`, which backOrder still reads whole). A pre-release kept leaf then reads as plain box:<tx> (Mint rank 2, after money others paid, as answer 4 places older entries). That alone also passes A, B and C, but classes D#0's way back as `lovejoin`, not `session:4`.

The policy's Lovejoin row ("the list of your mixes until their boxes are back") arguably covers it. If the owner counts it as a change in what's kept, add a clause to the unreleased 18 November entry.

5. Put tests A and C (and B, if the alternative is taken) beside 316#1's public test in tests/lovejoin-crediting-review-fixes.test.ts:386.

findings.title: money#4 and still#6 hold only for a choice the wallet can price: with a native reference script, Home and the forms still count 5 ₳ the builds never spend
findings.scenario: A 1.9.1 user pressed Set on a stranger's 5 ₳ (X) carrying a native reference script. Koios and the data layer give no native script's bytes (dapp.ts:3047-3048), so the wallet can't price spending X. Round two lists X as an ordinary row, flagged `unspendable: "script"` but not locked (:376). locked() now holds only Y, the 5 ₳ the builds put up, and Home's free figure is everything less what's locked (format.ts:454-461), so it counts X. So Max pays 5 ₳ less than 'Max, up to' said, its review listing X left out ('script'), and an amount in between passes the form only to be refused. Before round two, X was locked and Y counted as free: the same 5 ₳ gap, on the other UTxO. findings.who: A stranger (the 5 ₳ carrying a script), plus the user's 1.9.1 Set.
findings.evidence: coin-control.ts:352 `const collateral = collateralOf(choices, fresh, true)?.utxo;`; :376 `...(measurable(p.utxo) ? {} : script),` (a flag, not held); balances.ts:466 `const { lovelace, tokens } = sumValue(utxos.map((p) => p.utxo));`; build.rs:945-949 `let priced … .filter(|u| reference_script_size(u).is_ok())`; coin-control.test.ts:400 `["a reference script", { reference_script: { hash: "ab".repeat(28), size: 3, type: "timelock", bytes: "820080" } }]`.

That closes the same gap for any such UTxO, not only a 1.9.1 choice. Add `{ reference_script: { hash, size: null, type: "timelock", bytes: null } }` to SHAPES. Its 'Max spends own.utxos.length inputs' check fails today.

verdicts.evidence:
The finding holds on HEAD 5447f7e5. I traced it end to end and reproduced it with the real WebAssembly. It also reaches further than the finding says: no 1.9.1 Set is needed.

How the shape gets in. Koios and the data layer never give a native script's bytes. db-sync's `script.bytes` is null for timelock scripts, and seedelf-data/api/src/public/utxos.rs:211-218 passes it through as is; dapp.ts:3048 says the same. So `measurable` (koios.ts:92-97) is false for any native script. 1.9.1's Set could save such a 5 ₳ as the choice. At web-wallet/1.9.1, the candidate and the automatic pick were `isCollateralShaped` alone (1.9.1 coin-control.ts:205).

What the figures count (HEAD):
- listed() takes `collateralOf(choices, fresh, true)` (coin-control.ts:352). X fails collateralFits (:199, :226), so the pick is Y, the own 5 ₳.
- :374 marks only Y as locked. :376 gives X `unspendable: "script"`, which is a flag only.
- locked() sums `u.locked && !u.seedelf` (:298), giving 5 ₳ in 1 UTxO.
- The account's balance is every row (balances.ts:466). unlocked() takes off only `locked` (format.ts:454-461). Home.tsx:520-521 passes that to CardanoSend (:118 tooMuch, :341 "Max, up to") and to MoveIn (:66, :190). So X counts as free.

What the builds spend:
- readAccount → account(own) (account.ts:199, coin-control.ts:282-284) keeps only Y out, so X goes to WebAssembly.
- Core drops X: account_payment's `priced` (build.rs:945-949) and account_inputs (:3976). Max returns it as left_out with reason "script" (wasm lib.rs:172-183).

Guards I looked for:
- Max's review says "Max leaves 1 UTxO where it is: … holds a reference script the wallet can't spend" (en.json:895, :899).
- An amount in the gap is refused by publicShort with the true maximum.
- The Mix form leaves unspendable rows out (Lovejoin.tsx:415).
- Nothing subtracts an unspendable row from Home's figure or the forms' figures.
- The private side is already right: spendableOwned (balances.ts:515) leaves reference-script rows out of the private balance.

Run on HEAD (the test below): with the native choice, the forms' figure is 10473.014036 ₳ but Max spends 10468.014036 ₳ (7 of readAccount's 8 rows), a 5 ₳ gap. Send and Make private of the figure less 4 ₳ are refused ("can pay up to 10,465.688769 ₳"). Round two's own shape (a timelock with bytes "820080") passes, as the finding says. With 69d001e8's coin-control.ts swapped in, both choice shapes show the same 5 ₳ gap, on Y. That confirms "the same gap, on the other UTxO".

Wider than stated:
- A stranger's 5 ₳ with a native script, older than the account's own, and no choice at all shows the same 5 ₳ gap. 1.9.1 took that UTxO as the collateral, which kept it out of the figure. e8b#1's fix (2b3dfd80) stopped that, so chunk 51 opened this gap with no user action.
- Any unpriceable UTxO of another value had the gap already at 1.9.1. 1.9.1's listed() never held unspendable rows (1.9.1 coin-control.ts:322-324). A 10 ₳ one gives a 10 ₳ gap on HEAD.
- The round-two claims are wider than the code for this shape: architecture.md:378 ("so the forms' figures are what they spend"), flows.md:142 ("payments may spend it"), and coin-control.ts:270-273.

Why low: only figures are off, by the UTxO's value. The review shows the real amount and names the UTxO, an amount in the gap is refused in words with the true maximum, and nothing is lost or overpaid.
